Controlled via the keyboard, there are three levels of difficulty. Players have the option to allow incorrect or invalid values to be flagged.

210763.overview: A Christmas Adventure is a customizable adventure game by Bitcards, released just prior to Christmas 1983. You have been whisked to Santa's workshop to help him save Christmas. Typing simple two-word commands, you explore the workshop, defeat a few evil elves, and eventually save the holiday. The game was designed so that certain texts and graphics could be updated such that Santa explicitly calls on your gift recipient to save the day.

211346.overview: Computer Acquire is adapted from the board game Acquire by Avalon Hill. As in most games of high finance it is about making profits by buying low and selling high. Instead of the normal commodity or utility markets the simulation is based on hotel property stocks with mergers and hotel chaining. The goal is spotting the bargains early when the price is right along with adding more hotel chains to which you have controlling interest. Sprinkle in a little market luck along the way and win by becoming the wealthiest player. The game is turn based and allows you to play against the computer with up to six other players or allows the computer to play itself while you observe. The game has five skill levels and hotel chains have seven classes from moderate to prestigious. Each player starts with $6,000 and the game usually ends when one chain has at least 41 hotels.

213217.overview:
Artesians is a 1-player arcade game for the Apple II.

Driven by your desire for a special beer, you have been driven to don a burglar's mask and enter the secret Artesian Brewery. Once inside, you must gather empty bottles while heading to the 4th floor of the brewery, where you can fill your bottles with beer.

As you stalk through the brewery, you leave footprints behind. The clever canine Floyd can follow your footsteps, and if he tracks you down, he will begin to bark loudly and incessantly. Floyd can be distracted by dropping bones in the brewery, but his barking will arouse the watchman Old Hank from his slumber next to the fountain. Old Hank will descend his private elevator to your floor, and will attempt to apprehend you. If you are caught, you will be sentenced to 5 years of beerless jail time.

The Artesians roams about the brewery, and slow the player down. They are scared by light bulbs. The player can move in the 4 cardinal directions, and if they come in contact with a barrel, they will fall to a level below, and break their bottles. There are total of 4 levels of the brewery. On the first level, the player must travel through a tight maze. On the second layer, the player must cross fast moving conveyor belts, and on the third level, they must move on large gears. The player is victorious should they fill 4 bottles of beer.

214015.overview: Alter Ego is a game which tries to simulate life itself. The player creates a character with different personality statistics, either by assigning them randomly or by answering a few introductory questions. They then guide this character through seven life phases, from infancy to old age.

215956.overview:
Apple Graphics Games are a series of 10 games with hi-res graphics designed to teach the player how to program for the Apple II. The series comes with a manual fully documenting the coding for each game.

There are 10 games in total:
Match - The player attempts to match 30 different pieces with the 20 on a board. The player has a limited time, and scores a point for each piece successfully matched
Piano - The player creates a a song by typing notes onto sheet music. The song can be replayed at any time.
Pairs - A matching card game played on a large 14 x 10 grid
Catch - The player moves horizontally to try to catch balls as they drop from the sky
Boxes - Two players compete by attempting to draw boxes on a grid
Poker - 2-player 5 card stud poker game
Equate - 2 player math game, where players must search a large board of numbers for 3 numbers that provide the answer to the problem A x B +- C =
Spiral - The player has the computer draw a spiral my entering drawing instructions and number of repetitions
Lander - A Lunar Lander clone, where the player tries to land on columns by controlling the thrust of their landing craft
Spider - Arcade game where player controls a fly attempting to eat spider eggs

216646.overview:
This game was a recurring feature on several of Softdisk's disk subscriptions; each time it appeared on a particular platform, it contained different puzzles. It's a combination word game/sliding tile puzzle, in which letters must be manipulated and rearranged within a constrained area in order to spell out words. Several words can be worked on simultaneously, and the letters that appear in the last word of each set are determined by the positions of the letters in earlier words. 
 
Published in Softdisk Magazine issue 65 in 1987.

421463.overview: Airsim-1: Flight Simulator is a single player propeller based flight, simulation video game for Apple II E, published in 1981 by Mind Systems Corporation.

421487.overview:
Alibi is a text-based strategy game.

The Colonel has been murdered, and you are the detective who must determine when, where, and who committed the crime. The player must individually interview a number of suspect. The player can ask where they think each suspect was at a particular time or who was in a specific room at a particular time. The player must look for discrepancies between the different character's stories to determine who, when, and where the crime took place. The player has an infinite number of tries to report the crime correctly, and receives a final score based upon number of clues asked, number of times looking at notebook, and number of attempts to get the case correct.

There are 6 difficulty ranges from Constable to Chief Superintendent, which effect the number of suspects and the times in which the crime could have been committed.

421488.overview:
Alien Lander is a 1-player arcade game.

Player from a 1st person perspective, the player attempts to land on an alien surface, by controlling the speed of descent of their spaceship. The player can alter the gravity of the planet, strength of thrust, and density. The player has a limited amount of fuel, and must control when and how long they will burn fuel to try to make a soft landing. Gauges show remaining fuel, current velocity, altitude, and current time. If the player runs out of fuel, they hurtle towards the planet's surface.

421579.overview: World War III simulator. A clone of the game WarGames, which was also based on the movie of the same name.

421727.overview:
A game apparently developed by aliens, it was intercepted by the programmers at Southwestern Data Systems, whom were able to translate the game to work on Apple II computers, but were unable to convert the game text to English. In this game, the aliens are understandably depicted in the protagonist role, as they show their invasion of Earth.

In the first scene, the player controls an alien on the top of the screen, whom can move horizontally and fire vertically downwards. They player has to fire missiles at Earth shuttles and rockets which launch towards the player. The player gets points for destroying human vessel, and if a vessel manages to move past the player, the player's round is over, and they receive a score for this component. In the second game, the player can move in 4 cardinal directions, and must place landmines in the way of approaching human tanks. If the tank runs over a mine, it is destroyed. If the player runs into a tank while holding a mine, they lose a life and the tank is destroyed. The player has a total of 3 lives, and when all are lost it's game over.

422718.overview:
A.I. was one of the first pieces of educational software to explore pattern recognition and heuristic learning at a grade school level.

The premise of A.I. is that there is a simple go-like game board that players take turns placing pieces on until one manages to play a winning combination. The human player decides on the rules of the game first (i.e. four in a row horizontally wins) and then the A.I. learns the rules by playing the game and asking questions such as "have I won with this move?" Advanced players can then examine the routines that the AI used to study the rules and program in their own instructions for evaluating games. Although the package overplays the intelligence of the Apple II slightly, A.I. was still a surprisingly sophisticated set of learning algorithms for 1987.

422721.overview: Based on the board game of the same name, two or more players are required to build hotels along a boardwalk in Atlantic City, New Jersey. The hotels are constructed by placing markers that represent the growing floors of the hotels. The game progresses when players throw three dice, two standard numeric six-sided dice, and a special color die. The two numbers on the standard dice represents the total amount of money players can spend on construction, while the special die tells them that they can build in any color group. During the game, players can take over each other's hotels and get Fortune Cards, in which players can take advantage of construction bonuses, natural disasters, and other events to add and remove floors. As with the board game, the first player to pass $35 million in hotel property values wins the game.

422724.overview:
This computer game is based on the popular adult board game. Three to ten people can play, any of which can be computer controlled. Before the game starts, the human players determine their personality by giving scores to certain attributes. The computer's personalities are pre-determined. You can choose a picture of a face.

Each player has three to five dilemma cards and a single answer card. The responses are limited to yes or no. The objective of the game is to get rid of all your dilemma cards. You select an opponent to answer a card. If the player's answer and your answer card match, then they are both discarded. You are given a new answer card. Your strategy is to pick a person you know will give the answer you are looking for. If the answer doesn't match, the player is challenged. The remaining players vote on whether the answer given is true to their character or not. The winner of the challenge gives a dilemma card to the loser.

The graphics are limited to just showing the questions, your cards and the other players faces.

424007.overview:
A Stellar Trek is an early Star Trek variant for the Apple II.

The player takes control of the Enterprise, as they try to destroy all Klingon vessels located in a 64 quadrant galaxy that is further divided into 10 x 10 sectors. The galaxy included Federations and Romulan starbases, stars, planets, and black holes. The player controls all ship functions, including: movement via warp and impulse engines, use of starship weaponry, maintenance of energy reserves, and repair of incurred damage. The player has access to short ranges scanners which investigate the nearby sectors and long range scanners that provide limited information on surrounding quadrants. Local planets can be mined for dilithium to increase energy. There are 5 levels of difficulty and 3 game lengths available.

447495.overview:
Apple Casino is a compilation of four BASIC games:

-  Stars
-  Acey-Ducey
-  Slot Machine
-  Black Hole

447572.overview: Play music on your Apple II. Developed by Shin Katsumata, and published by Powersoft in 1978.

448944.overview: The player takes on the role of an air traffic controller, who tries to guide 10 planes or helicopters towards a safe landing on a landing strip. The landing strip and planes are graphically displayed on the screen from a top-down point of view. To control planes, the player must select individual planes, and can tell them what direction to travel, and whether to ascend, descend, or level out. Planes automatically switch to landing mode when they descend beneath 200 feet and attempt to land, and all other planes become locked out from player control. To successfully land a plane, it must descend on the east third of the runway and be travelling west. The player can receive a computer read out at any time of all planes and their current direction and altitude. Intermittently a plane can either be hijacked or have their engine fall off. This situation must be quickly remedied, or the plane will crash. If a plane leaves the screen, a new plane on a landing trajectory will replace it. Planes can be lost by striking other planes, or hitting the ground not going the correct direction on the runway. UFOs cannot be controlled, but pose a danger to other aircraft.

455843.overview:
Compilation of 2 previously released compilations:

* Arcade Games
* Sports Spectacular

455847.overview:
Compilation of three games:

1) Super Stomper
2) Mutant
3) Parachutist

457076.overview:
Aussie Joker Poker is a point scoring card game for 2-90 players.

Each player is dealt a hand of five cards, and the hand is scored according to poker hand value, card value, and the suits involved.

After being dealt a hand, the player is displayed a score. The player can risk discarding cards to acquire a better hand, but if the point value is lessened, the player busts, and they forfeit points for that hand. The player can keep risking drawing new cards to improve their hand until they bust or are satisfied with their score.

Card are selecting using the numbers one to five, and they are graphically displayed on the screen. There is an option to display who the current leading hand is each round, and the score to beat. The player can define the number of rounds per game.

457106.overview:
Saturn Navigator is an entry in subLOGIC's Flight Simulator series (A2-3DA) and considered an expansion to the original game, though it is a stand-alone title that does not require the original Flight Simulator disk to function. It simulates a trip from Earth in a rocket-propelled spacecraft to rendezvous with an imaginary Saturn-orbiting space station.

The game is extremely complex and based around scientific principles of spaceflight. It was actually created by a scientist at Jet Propulsion Laboratories. The four stages of the game are: Transorbit, Approach, Orbit and Rendezvous.

460353.overview:
Anchorman is a 1–2 player bowling game for the Apple II.

A ten pin or shorter duck pins game, the player bowls by choosing the location of their bowl and the spin. An animated character moves across the screen, where their speed controls the strength of ball release. An animation from the view of the bowler shows the pin position and ball movement.

The player can choose spare time, splits, wash, match game, or anchorman. The program tracks records over multiple games. Allows for play against two human opponents or a computer opponent with five levels of difficulty.

461410.overview:
A compilation of 4 Arcade style games.

1) D-Day

2) Shark Bait

3) Bee Crunch

4) Formula Racer
